chunks: About the Descendents (‘Itrah) of the Holy Prophet: “So wither are you going to”?
and “how are you then turned away?”
Ensigns (of guidance) are standing, indications (of virtue) are clear, and the minarets (of light) have been fixed. Where are you being taken astray?
How are you groping while you have among you the descendents of the Prophet?
They are the reins of Right, ensigns of Faith and tongues of truth!
According to them the same good position as you accord to the Qur’ān, and come to them (for quenching the thirst of guidance) as the thirsty camels approach the water spring.

key_terms.أَنَّىٰ تُؤْفَكُونَ: how are you then turned away (Quranic verse)
key_terms.فَأَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ: So wither are you going to (Quranic verse)
key_terms.وُرُودَ الْهِيمِ: The approach of the thirsty camel

ai.seo_question: How does Nahj al-Balagha describe the status of the Prophet's Descendents (Ahl al-Bayt) in relation to the Qur'an?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali uses rhetorical questions to highlight the clarity of the 'Itrah as the 'lamps of guidance' amidst the confusion of the believers. He emphasizes their role as the 'bridles of truth' and commands the community to revere them with the intensity of the 'thirsty camel' (al-him al-'ishash), a metaphor for urgent spiritual need. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that the Ahl al-Bayt are the living embodiment of the Quran's guidance, essential for navigating religious certainty.
